long_biography.plain_text:
Insurance executive Jeffrey B. Scott studies investments by examining the businesses behind lenders' portfolios. His research into artificial intelligence's effect on private credit compared four business development companies, using their annual filings to assess borrowers individually. He separated software companies by their exposure to disruption and by protections such as proprietary data, regulation and established customer workflows.

Scott built spreadsheet models that tested possible loan losses against the higher interest rates lenders might obtain when refinancing borrowers. He varied the timing and severity of losses across scenarios and offered readers editable models. He disclosed personal investments in the companies he examined.
